label: Love and devotion
title: Bhagavad Gita on Bhakti: 7 Verses on Love and Devotion
description: Seven verses on loving Krishna, from 'all four kinds are welcome' (7.16) to 'you are dear to me' (18.65). Sanskrit, plain English and one simple practice with each.
h1: Bhagavad Gita on bhakti: 7 verses on love and devotion
subtitle: For when you want to feel close to Krishna. Read one a day, or all seven at your altar.
keywords: bhagavad gita on love for god
intro: Bhakti is the warmest thread in the Gita. Krishna says people come to him in distress, in curiosity, in need or in wisdom, and all four are welcome (7.16). These verses walk through his promises: he lives in those who love him (9.29), he lifts them out of the drowning sea (12.7), he gives them the understanding to reach him (10.10). Then they turn to practice: offer everything (9.27), and keep your mind on him, because you are dear to him (18.65). The last is from the Ramcharitmanas, Ram at Shabari's door.

days.heading: Every reason is welcome
days.line: People turn to the divine in distress, in curiosity, in need, or in wisdom. All four are welcome.
days.forYou: You may come to Krishna because something hurts, because you're curious, because you need something, or because you understand. Krishna calls all four sukṛtinaḥ, good people. Whatever brought you here counts.
days.today: Name, honestly, which of the four brings you here today.

days.heading: He lives in those who love him
days.line: I am the same towards all; no one is hated, no one favoured. Those who love me live in me.
days.forYou: Krishna holds no favourites and no grudges. Love is the one thing that changes the relationship: those who love him live in him, and he in them.
days.today: Spend two quiet minutes today simply thinking of Krishna, asking for nothing.

days.heading: Lifted out of the sea
days.line: Whoever rests their heart in me, I lift out of the drowning sea, and soon.
days.forYou: Krishna's promise here is personal and quick: acirāt, soon. Whoever rests their heart in him, he lifts out of the sea of birth and death. Devotion in the Gita comes with being held.
days.today: When something worries you today, say his name once and breathe out.

days.heading: He gives the understanding
days.line: To those who keep loving me, I give the clarity that brings them to me.
days.forYou: Krishna says he himself gives buddhi-yoga, the right understanding, to those who stay devoted. You don't have to work out the whole path alone. Keep loving, and the clarity comes.
days.today: Read one verse of the Gita slowly today, and sit with it before moving on.

days.heading: Make everything an offering
days.line: Whatever you do, eat, give or endure, do it as an offering.
days.forYou: Krishna widens bhakti to cover the whole day: work, meals, gifts, hardships. Each can be offered to him. Your ordinary day becomes the worship.
days.today: Before one routine task today, offer it to Krishna in a single sentence.

days.heading: You are dear to me
days.line: Mind on me, heart devoted to me, you will come to me. I promise: you are dear to me.
days.forYou: Near the end of the Gita, Krishna makes a promise to Arjuna and calls it true: priyo 'si me, you are dear to me. Devotion runs both ways. He loves you back.
days.today: Light a lamp or sit at your altar today, and read this verse aloud.

days.heading: Ram at Shabari's door

story.title: Ram visits Shabari
story.body: Shabari was an old forest woman who had waited for Ram for years. When he finally came, she washed his feet and fed him the roots and fruit she had gathered, and he praised every bite. Then Ram told her he recognised only one bond, the bond of devotion, and described nine forms of it. The eighth was being content with what comes and never looking for faults in others.
story.lesson: What counts is the heart you bring.

verse.sanskrit: आठवँ जथालाभ संतोषा । सपनेहुँ नहिं देखइ परदोषा ॥
verse.line: Be content with what comes, and don't go looking for faults in others, not even in your dreams.

days.forYou: Shabari had no learning or status to offer, only years of waiting and a basket of fruit. Ram said that was enough.
days.today: Offer one simple thing to Krishna today, a flower, a fruit or a little water.

faq.q: What does the Bhagavad Gita say about devotion?
faq.a: Chapters 9 and 12 are the heart of bhakti in the Gita. Krishna says those who love him live in him (9.29), that he lifts them out of the sea of death (12.7), and in 18.65 he promises Arjuna that he is dear to him.

faq.q: Which Gita verse is about offering everything to God?
faq.a: 9.27: whatever you do, eat, offer, give or endure, do it as an offering to me. 9.26 adds that a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water offered with love is accepted.

faq.q: What are the nine forms of devotion Ram describes?
faq.a: In the Ramcharitmanas, Ram tells Shabari of navadhā bhakti, nine forms: good company, love for his stories, serving the teacher, singing his praise, chanting his name, self-restraint, seeing him in everything, contentment without fault-finding, and simplicity.
